newsitem.title: RUSSIA: CIS summit put off after Yeltsin's illness.
newsitem.headline: CIS summit put off after Yeltsin's illness.

text.p: A Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) summit scheduled for Moscow on January 17, which Russian President Boris Yeltsin had been due to attend, has been postponed, Interfax news agency said on Friday.

Interfax gave no reason for the postponement until January 30-31. But it appeared likely that the decision had been taken because Yeltsin has pneumonia and his illness would have prevented him attending.
Interfax later quoted Ivan Korotchenya, secretary of the organisation grouping 12 of the 15 former Soviet republics, as saying Yeltsin had asked other CIS leaders to put off the summit.
Korotchenya cited several reasons given by Yeltsin in his written request, including organisational problems, but said Yeltsin's illness was not among them.
Yeltsin was admitted to hospital on Wednesday night, only two weeks after returning to work following a major heart operation on November 5.
Doctors treating Yeltsin said on Friday he was breathing more easily but there had been no dramatic improvement in his condition, the Kremlin said.
